name: Olusegun Brandt-Mirzoyan
creator: Olusegun Brandt-Mirzoyan
description: Dead since 2198, Brandt-Mirzoyan published exactly one book during his lifetime — 'The Patience of Rust' (2191), a novel about a Shelf demolition crew that discovers the building they are contracted to destroy contains a sealed room with forty years of someone's private journals. He died in a transit accident that was ruled accidental and disputed ever since. In the twenty-five years since his death, three additional manuscripts have surfaced through different channels, each contested as authentic or fabricated, each adding new dimensions to his themes of buried testimony and institutional erasure.
medium: original physical print (extremely scarce); neural feed editions produced posthumously by a Shelf preservation collective
cultural_impact: Brandt-Mirzoyan has become a Shelf legend to an extent that complicates honest assessment of his actual work. His name is invoked in Shelf rights organizing, in art, in graffiti. Whether the posthumous manuscripts are real or fabricated has become almost secondary to what they represent — the idea that a Shelf writer's full work can be suppressed and only partially recovered.
controversy: The third posthumous manuscript, surfacing in 2221, contains passages that appear to describe his own death in detail — written, if authentic, three weeks before the transit accident. A corponation security firm has acquired what it claims are the original files and refuses to release them for authentication. Two separate groups claim to hold his literary estate.
story_hooks: A fourth manuscript has surfaced and the players are hired to authenticate it — the content, if real, names a specific corponation executive in connection with Brandt-Mirzoyan's death.
The sealed room from 'The Patience of Rust' appears to be based on a real location — and someone has been quietly looking for it for years.

One of the two groups claiming his literary estate is run by people who were children when he died and claim to be his family — the other is a corponation cultural archive subsidiary, and the legal battle will determine whether his work becomes public or proprietary.
